The dataset we use is from the Contagio Archive... We use 5,586 malicious and 4,476 benign PDF files for training

we compute the proportion of 100 malicious test seed PDFs for which EvadeML successfully evades the classifier
unresolved: n_seeds left null: the paper's '40/100 seeds' refers to malicious PDF seed files used to generate evasion instances, not repetition/random seeds for statistical variance; no repeated-trial or random-seed count is stated for the ML training itself.

n_baselines set to 3 (original undefended classifier, RAR, FSR) as the core comparison arms against the proposed CFR method; the paper also reports several ablation/ancillary classifiers (CF-only, l1-regularized Linear, single-feature JS, and the CFR-JS expert-feature variant) that could arguably also count as baselines/comparison points depending on definition.

n_eval_types set to 2 per the paper's own explicit framing ('We evaluate performance in two ways'), though within 'traditional evaluation' it separately reports ROC/AUC and also TPR/FPR/FNR at fixed thresholds.
No confidence intervals, standard deviations, or multi-run statistics are reported anywhere; all robustness/AUC figures appear to be single-run point estimates presented as bar/ROC figures.

'control_arm' coded as 'clean' because the paper's 'non-adversarial test data' ROC/AUC evaluation serves as the clean-performance reference arm alongside the adversarial evasion-robustness evaluation; this is not a poisoning-defense clean/backdoor control in the strict sense, since this paper is about test-time evasion, not training-time backdoors.
